notes: Lists has a new example: things you drag onto slots, with a swap and dragging off to empty a slot.
The Item cards specimen shows icons before some of the stats, plain and in a skin.
The Item cards specimen shows the effect box's edge, plain and in a skin's colour.
The Item cards specimen has the badges beside the title and stats that grow per level.
New specimen: Game covers, a game's tall cover with late art, its tile when there is none, and a spinner while it is added.
New specimen: Item cards, the tooltip's card in a panel, plain and in a module's skin.
The Select examples show a long choice wrapped between words, and a name that changes shows at once.
The map and zoom examples keep their last view when Tavora closes or sleeps.
New specimen: Why it is off, a reason on a switched-off switch, box, field, select, button and menu row.
New specimens: a line chart with one or two lines over game time or dates, its tooltip, and its empty and one-point states.
The slider with its value now shows an editable box and a Reset button, with specimens for each, narrow and in German.
New specimen: segmented control with icons, icon-only options and one option that is off with a reason.
New specimens: a data grid you can type into like a spreadsheet, and a read-only one with 5,000 rows.
Wide buttons and pickers only dip 1px when pressed.
Under the hood: newer libraries.
The zoom specimens now include one that hides and shows the pane, and maps keep their view when you switch tabs or close a dialog.
New page: Overlay text, the box every overlay text uses, with scrolling, shrinking and cutting off, and its settings.
New specimen: rows you drag to reorder.
Loads a little lighter: the app keeps only the Latin letters of its fonts.
New specimen: a field with a list of suggestions where you can type your own text (Combobox with free text).
Dialogs you open with the keyboard appear instantly.
Toasts wait while the panel is hidden or the game is in front, and slide in and out from their edge.
Settings shows a dialog with one page and one with several pages, with the rules for descriptions and units.
New specimens: a settings menu with Overlays, and text with placeholders.
The settings dialog example uses the same menu and has a Delete row.
The Foundations pages are filled: colours, text, spacing and corners, motion and writing, each with live examples and their code.
Show disabled sits in the page header for everyone; the Developer tools switch is gone.
Show code is coloured and has line numbers; Copy still copies the plain code. Examples no longer carry any Show disabled code, so what you see is what you write.
New specimen: Delete with Undo, gone at once and back with Undo.
Screen readers read each message once.

Pan and zoom and the tile map show the new shared controls: zoom, the % (back to 100 %), the whole map and your own buttons, double-click to zoom in, a canvas that draws itself, a tooltip next to a node, and a view that is remembered.
A side menu with search and one page per kind of control. Every example shows its own code, and the developer helpers sit behind a switch.

Lists open under their field and are at least as wide; the combobox has a clear button; the picture select no longer shows the toggle examples inside its list; the tab row no longer shows a scrollbar.
Main buttons and badges can follow a theme's deeper button colour.
The UI Playground shows loading placeholders and pictures that fade in.
Lists, dialogs and settings pages move smoothly.
Switches and tabs slide to what you pick.
New specimens: a button that shows its own progress, and numbers that count to their new value.
Buttons have a little depth and feel pressed when you click them.
Checkboxes, toggles and options animate when you pick them, and folding sections open smoothly.
Dialogs have an icon box, a short line under the title, a Close button in the corner and footer buttons that carry an icon only when they do something. New specimens show it.
Menus and tooltips open out of the spot they belong to, and buttons dip a little when you press them.
A disabled button with a tooltip still shows it, so you can see why it is off.
Dropdowns where you pick a value show an up-and-down arrow, menus keep the down arrow. Both are side by side in Inputs.
The tile map shows a layer over the map and under the pins, such as a fog of war.
Text fields and dropdowns look calmer in Dark mode.
Patch notes for this module start with this version.
